key_insight: The paper introduces a high-order finite-difference framework for relativistic hydrodynamics that preserves physical admissibility by turning nonlinear positivity and subluminal-velocity constraints into solvable linear inequalities.
engineering_relevance: This gives CFD practitioners a more robust way to simulate shocks and extreme flows without numerical breakdown, while retaining high-order accuracy for smooth regions.
method: Uses a GQL reformulation to convert relativistic constraint handling into a family of linear conditions.
Integrates a Zalesak-type flux-corrected transport limiter directly on conservative variables.
Computes limiter parameters non-iteratively via small symmetric eigenvalue problems, with relaxed multidimensional variants for lower cost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive tests from 1D to 3D, including ultra-relativistic Riemann problems and astrophysical jets, showing stable constraint enforcement, sharp discontinuity resolution, and design-order accuracy on smooth solutions.
watch_item: The eigenvalue-based limiter is efficient but still adds implementation complexity, especially in multidimensional cases where relaxed variants are used to reduce cost.
paper_title: GQL-Based Physical-Constraint-Preserving High-Order Finite Difference Schemes for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Arbitrary Dimensions
